source_row.extraction_instructions: NOT YET SCRAPABLE — www.rcoa.ac.uk sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge (interstitial 'Just a moment…' / chl_page orchestrate) that headless Chromium never clears; leave active=false until a non-headless or allowlisted fetch path exists. Structure recorded from a one-off headed browser session for whoever revisits: Drupal 'view-events' listing, 9 cards per page, zero-indexed pager ?page=0..3 (~36-40 upcoming events); cards carry title, date, city and CPD credits. Detail URLs are /events/<slug>. Detail pages use Overview/Programme/Pricing tabs — fees live on the Pricing tab, not the overview, so pricing needs the tab-aware fetch pattern (cf. rcr.py). Mix of conferences, revision courses, webinars and study days.
source_row.notes_blocked: Do not wire into the daily matrix. Also note the pager is 0-indexed, so the standard page_query walker (starts at n=1) would silently skip the first 9 events even once access is solved.

registry_comment: RCoA (40) — NOT REGISTERED: Cloudflare managed challenge blocks headless Chromium (403 on every path). See Conference_masterlist/wave1c/rcoa.json.

blocking_evidence.challenge_type: Cloudflare managed challenge — non-interactive JS interstitial, title 'Just a moment...', body 'Performing security verification', script /cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/h/b/orchestrate/chl_page/v1?ray=...
blocking_evidence.headless_playwright: BLOCKED. Project BrowserController (browser.py, chromium.launch(headless=True), launch flags unchanged) → page.goto('https://www.rcoa.ac.uk/events', wait_until='load') returns HTTP 403. Body is the 28.6 KB interstitial.
blocking_evidence.longer_wait_helps: No. Polled page.content() every 5 s for 60 s: HTML length settled at 28,613 chars after the first second and never changed; title stayed 'Just a moment...' for the entire 60 s. A second headless run polling 8 s per URL gave the same result.
blocking_evidence.scope_of_block_headless: Whole domain, not just the listing. Headless 403 + interstitial on https://www.rcoa.ac.uk/events, https://www.rcoa.ac.uk/, https://www.rcoa.ac.uk/robots.txt, and on two detail pages (/events/anaesthesia-2027, /events/anaesthetists-educators-programme).
blocking_evidence.curl: 403 both with default curl UA and with the project's spoofed Chrome 124 desktop UA — matches recon.
blocking_evidence.non_headless_one_off: CLEARS IMMEDIATELY (informational only, run once locally on a home IP). chromium.launch(headless=False) → /events returned HTTP 200, real title '| The Royal College of Anaesthetists', 287,623 chars, 9 event cards and pager links page=0..3 present on first paint with no visible challenge step. So the discriminator is the headless flag / headless browser fingerprint, not the IP address and not a login wall. Curiously the same headed session still got 403 on / and /robots.txt, so the edge rule is not uniform across paths.
blocking_evidence.not_attempted: No stealth plugins, no patched-Chromium/undetected driver, no third-party CAPTCHA/bypass service, no launch-flag changes to browser.py — per brief.

concerns: Recon record for this domain is WRONG on the decisive point: it claims 'headless Playwright loads fine'. It does not — headless gets a 403 interstitial on every path tested. Any other wave-1c source whose recon says 'js_required, browser works' on a Cloudflare domain should be re-verified the same way before a build agent is spent on it.

No extractor file was written. medconf-scraper/extractors/rcoa.py does NOT exist — building it would mean shipping code that cannot be tested by the harness or run in CI. All structural findings needed to write it later are captured in source_row.extraction_instructions above.

An alternative non-browser surface is unlikely to help: the Cloudflare rule fires at the edge for the whole host (robots.txt itself 403s), so a Drupal JSON:API / views-REST / RSS endpoint on www.rcoa.ac.uk would be challenged identically. Not probed further, to stay inside the polite request budget.

If this source is wanted later, the realistic options are (a) ask RCoA to allowlist the scraper's CI egress or provide a feed, (b) a headful browser in CI (xvfb + headless=False), or (c) a residential-IP/headful runner. (b) is the cheapest to test but is a browser.py / workflow change, which this agent is not permitted to make and which would affect all 39 other sources — it should be a deliberate, separately-owned decision.
Pager is 0-indexed (?page=0 is page one). The shared page_query walker starts at n=1, so even after access is solved this source needs either a pagination_template offset or a list_shells_override.
Total requests to rcoa.ac.uk during this investigation: ~15 page loads. No database, git, or shared-file changes were made.
